results.note: si.edu blocks the WebFetch agent (403) but served the page to a plain browser fetch (HTTP 200). Page reads 'Over the past forty years, a diverse Taíno movement has taken form' and names Cuba, the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico; evidence phrase verbatim. Exhibition dated July 28, 2018 to Nov 12, 2019, so as_of 2018 holds.

smithsonianmag.com blocks WebFetch (403) but served to a browser fetch (200). Article says community efforts 'include language research ... explore the Taíno roots of familiar words (terms such as hurricane, hammock and tobacco have been credited to Taíno)'. Evidence verbatim; own words.

Same article: 'In the tristate area of New York, the Arawak Mountain Singers formed in 1991 and grew active in the powwow circuit'; other diaspora groups (Pittsburgh 1982, Bronx yukayeke) named alongside. Evidence verbatim.

PDF text extracted locally (pdftotext). Statement names 'our very own Indigenous Groups including the Santa Rosa First Peoples Community ... and Warao Nation of Trinidad and Tobago' and 'The annual Day of Recognition, celebrated on October 14 every year'. Evidence verbatim. Issued by the Permanent Mission of T&T to the OAS, hosted on foreign.gov.tt, dated Aug 9, 2018.

National Trust page (Oct 20, 2020) names Nepoyo and Carinepogoto as the peoples the community celebrates descent from, mentions 'a week of cultural events and displays involving the public' and the October 14 commemoration. Evidence verbatim.

Page says culture is 'passed down to newer generation and the wider public' and calls the community 'the official preservation and cultural ambassadors for their community'. Evidence verbatim; as_of 2020 matches article date.
Ministry page: 'located in the Upper Mazaruni area, on the Barama, Upper Pomeroon, Demerara Wenamu, and the Upper Cuyuni rivers'. Fact omits Demerara, which is a harmless omission. Evidence verbatim.

minorityrights.org blocks WebFetch and curl (403); page read through the real browser pane (200). Page uses only the spelling 'Kapohn' ('originally called themselves Kapohn'; heading 'Kapohn (Akawaio)'; 'The Kapohn like most of the interior tribes are Carib speakers'). The spelling 'Kapon' does not appear on this page, so the 'also written' clause was removed and the Carib claim aligned to the page's wording. Evidence verbatim.
results.text: Kapohn is the Akawaio people's own name for themselves, and like most peoples of Guyana's interior they are Carib speakers.
results.evidence: The Kapohn like most of the interior tribes are Carib speakers

results.note: DPI article (July 13, 2021) lists exactly nine languages incl. Akawaio and says funds will be budgeted to 'restart this project'. Evidence verbatim.
Ministry page: 'mainly in the Northern Pakaraimas Mountains, as well as in the South Pakaraimas and the Essequibo region'. Evidence verbatim.

Cultural Survival Quarterly (May 7, 2010): 'Chenapou, the Patamona village closest to the park' and 'wider Patamona communities who depend on the area in and around Kaieteur to hunt, fish, gather plants'. Evidence verbatim; as_of 2010 matches.

ISA Taurepang page: 'two major ethnic groups: the Pemon and the Kapon ... the latter of the Ingarikó and Patamona'; Ingarikó identified as the Akawaio in Brazil near the Guyana frontier. Evidence verbatim. 'Border region' is the page's circum-Roraima setting; acceptable.
ISA page: 'The Taurepang refer to themselves as Pemon, a term meaning people or us' and Pemon 'is the self-designation of the Arekuna, Kamarakoto, Taurepang and Macuxi'. Evidence verbatim.

INE PDF extracted locally: 2011 census, 52 pueblos, 'wayuu (57,05%), warao (6,73%), kariña (4,67%) y pemón (4,16%)' as shares of the Indigenous population; table note says ethnonyms were those used by declarants 'para su autorreconocimiento'. Evidence verbatim (diacritics intact in source).
Ministry page Arecuna entry: 'this tribe is located on the banks of the Kamarang river'. Evidence verbatim.

PAC page: 'the Wai Wai took the bold step in 2007 to designate their land a Community Owned Conservation Area (COCA)' and 'In August 2017, the Government of Guyana legally gazetted the area declaring it a National Protected Area'; land held under 'absolute title'. Evidence verbatim.
Ministry page: 'skilled architects of indigenous dwelling were fittingly tasked with the construction of the landmark Umana Yana. Expert weavers and bead designers...'. Evidence verbatim.

ISA Waiwai page: Waiwai is 'a member of the Karib language family' and 'the main language used by the inhabitants of the Waiwai communities'; 'the majority of young people born in the Waiwai communities speak only this dominant language' where the dominant language is Waiwai. Evidence verbatim.
INE PDF: 'warao (6,73%)' among the 2011 census shares of the Indigenous population; self-identification noted in table footnote. Evidence verbatim.
Ministry page Warrau entry: 'lives in the swamps and marshes of the North West District, in the low-lying areas of the Barima and Pomeroon rivers and their tributaries'. Evidence verbatim.
T&T statement PDF names 'Warao Nation of Trinidad and Tobago' among 'our very own Indigenous Groups'. Evidence verbatim; as_of 2018 matches statement date.

ISA Tiriyó page: 'they generally identify themselves as Wü Tarëno (I am Tarëno), by which they mean: I am from here, from this region'; 'this denomination was given to them by the whites'; groups 'grouped under the name Tiriyó in Brazil, and Trio in Suriname' by missionaries. Evidence verbatim.
VIDS page: 'Suriname is het woongebied van vier grote Inheemse volken ... Trio (Tiriyo, Tarëno) en Wayana' and 'de Wayana en Trio voornamelijk in het zuiden'. Evidence verbatim.
ISA page: Tiriyó with Katxuyana, Txikuyana, Wayana and Aparai 'inhabit the Tumucumaque Indigenous Park, ratified in 1997 through Decree 213'; 'The area covers 3,071,067 ha'. Evidence verbatim.

ISA Wayana intro lists Brazil (East Paru), Surinam (Tapanahoni and Paloemeu rivers) and 'French Guiana (upper Maroni River and its tributaries the Tampok and Marouini)'. Evidence verbatim. 'Southern Suriname' is a fair gloss of the Tapanahoni/Paloemeu location.

ISA Language section, about the Aparai-Wayana population of the East Paru in Brazil: 'the Wayana language has gained an enormous prestige among the younger people' because it links them to Wayana and Tiriyó in Surinam and French Guiana. Evidence verbatim.

Ministère de la Culture PDF (Bilan au 7 décembre 2015) extracted locally: '6 langues amérindiennes (toutes Langues de France)' incl. wayana; list of 12 Langues de France contains the evidence phrase verbatim.
Parc amazonien page: 'Les Amérindiens Teko sont quant à eux présents sur ces deux bassins de vie (Cayodé sur le haut Maroni et Camopi sur l'Oyapock)'. Evidence verbatim.

Parc amazonien page: 'les langues amérindiennes se partagent en deux groupes. Les langues wayãpi et teko appartiennent à la famille linguistique Tupi-Guarani. La langue wayana appartient ... à la famille linguistique caribe'. Evidence verbatim.
Culture ministry PDF lists under the six Amerindian Langues de France: 'teko (anciennement émerillon)'. Evidence verbatim.
ISA Wajãpi page: 'In 1994 ... the self-demarcation of the Wajãpi Indigenous Land began' and 'In the same year, the Council of Wajãpi Villages was founded ... also called Apina'. Evidence verbatim.

UNESCO ICH page: 'Inscribed in 2008 (3.COM) on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (originally proclaimed in 2003)'; 'This graphic art is known as kusiwa'. Evidence verbatim in rendered text.
Parc amazonien page: 'les Wayãpi se répartissent entre le moyen et le haut Oyapock'. Evidence verbatim.

ISA Palikur page: 'The Palikur speak Parikwaki, a language affiliated to the Arawak language family' and 'the Palikur use the term Parikwene, the people of the river of the middle'. Evidence verbatim.
ISA page: 'Presently, the Palikur have villages in both Brazil and French Guiana and constantly transit across the border'; crossings 'to conduct commerce, visit kin'. Evidence verbatim.
Culture ministry PDF lists 'parikwaki (palikur)' among the six Amerindian Langues de France. Evidence verbatim.

INE PDF: 'el pueblo que se auto-denomina ye'kwana. Este término apareció por primera vez en el censo de 1982 y se impuso en los censos posteriores, eliminando casi totalmente el nombre de makiritare'; footnote says Makiritare came from neighbouring peoples. Evidence verbatim.
ISA Ye'kwana page: 'they use the word So'to, which can be translated as people, person' and 'Ye'kuana ... can be translated as canoe people'. Evidence verbatim (curly apostrophe as on page).

ISA page: 'divided amongst three communities located on the banks of the Auaris and Uraricoera rivers'; region 'demarcated in the 1990s, as Yanomami Indian Land. The three Ye'kuana communities are included in this area.' Roraima named. Evidence verbatim.

INE PDF: 'algunos pueblos no usan todavía su auto-denominación, a veces por la dificultad que representa para los no-indígenas su pronunciación como piaroa en lugar de wótüja (palabra que tiene además varias grafías según las comunidades)'. The source does not say 'many'; it attributes the use of Piaroa to pronunciation difficulty for non-Indigenous people. Text tightened to that. Evidence verbatim.
results.text: Venezuela's statistics institute notes that Piaroa is still used instead of the people's own name, Wótüja, a word non-Indigenous speakers find hard to say and that communities spell in several ways.
results.evidence: su pronunciación como piaroa en lugar de wótüja

results.note: Pronunciamiento PDF extracted locally: 'la lucha por la defensa de nuestro territorio se inició en el Primer Congreso del Pueblo Indígena Uwottüja en 1984, con el eslogan como una sola churuata y con una sola voz defendamos nuestras tierras ancestrales'. Evidence verbatim.

Same PDF: title names the four rivers and Orinoco Medio; 'reunidos en la Comunidad Pendare'; 'reconocemos que somos herederos, poseedores y guardianes de nuestros territorios' and demand to be recognized 'como guardianes de los territorios de los cuatro ríos'. Year 2020 supported by the document's own reference to 02/03/2020 and file date Feb 29, 2020. Evidence verbatim.

MinCultura PDF extracted locally: 'la lengua yukpa pertenece a la familia lingüística caribe'; 'en alto grado de vitalidad, pues es la lengua de comunicación cotidiana'; 'en la mayoría de los pueblos los hablantes del yukpa se comunican en lengua vernácula y se preocupan de que sus niños lo aprendan'. Evidence verbatim.

Same PDF: 'en Colombia, los yukpa están organizados en resguardos, cada uno formado por asentamientos ... Existe un cabildo mayor, representante ante el Gobierno, y cada asentamiento ... es liderado por un cabildo menor'. Evidence verbatim.

minorityrights.org blocks WebFetch/curl (403); read through the browser pane (200): 'At the time of the 2011 Census in Venezuela and the 2018 Census in Colombia ... the Yukpa people included around 10,640 in Venezuela and 3,610 in Colombia'. Evidence verbatim.

MinCultura Barí PDF extracted locally: 'Su lengua pertenece a la familia lingüística chibcha ... la lengua barí se está transmitiendo a las nuevas generaciones, y tiene hablantes de todas las edades'. Evidence verbatim.

Same PDF: 'en el departamento de Norte de Santander, en las estribaciones de la Serranía de los Motilones, en las hoyas de los ríos Catatumbo y Oro; hay también asentamientos de población barí en Venezuela en el estado Zulia'. Evidence verbatim.
MRG page via browser pane: 'the Barí people comprised approximately 2,841 individuals in Venezuela and 3,018 in Colombia' at the 2011 (VE) and 2018 (CO) censuses. Evidence verbatim.

AGN article dated 20 May 2024: 'El Parlamento del Pueblo Xinka recibió al presidente de la República, Bernardo Arévalo, en el departamento de Santa Rosa'; event 'en la aldea San Juan de Arana, del municipio de Cuilapa'; convenio 'establece 13 puntos'. Evidence verbatim.

USAC DIGI PDF extracted locally: language rescue effort is 'un esfuerzo conjunto entre la Cooperativa El Recuerdo, el Consejo del Pueblo Xinka de Guatemala (COPXIG) y el acompañamiento técnico pedagógico de la Dirección Departamental de Educación, con sede en Cuilapa, Santa Rosa'. Evidence verbatim.

Same PDF: identity markers are 'fundamentalmente el mantenimiento de sus tierras comunales y de las organizaciones sociales que sirven para administrarlas'; study region covers Santa Rosa, Jalapa and Jutiapa. Evidence verbatim.

ALMG grammar PDF extracted locally: 'Los municipios que conforman la comunidad lingüística Ch'orti', se encuentran: Jocotán, Camotán, Olopa, Quezaltepeque en el departamento de Chiquimula, y La Unión del departamento de Zacapa'. Evidence verbatim.
AGN article dated 15 Sept 2025: ALMG 'ha dado un paso importante al traducir los símbolos patrios a este idioma maya'; 'la bandera de Guatemala se traduce como tz'apray b'ujk'. Evidence verbatim.
AGN article dated 5 Feb 2025: 'así como en comunidades hondureñas como Cabañas, Santa Rita y Copán Ruinas'. Evidence verbatim.

names.note: Smithsonian exhibition page uses 'Taíno' with the accent; no single official body, official_url null is honest.
T&T government statement names 'Santa Rosa First Peoples Community' exactly.
Ministry of Amerindian Affairs lists 'Akawaios'; self-name Kapohn/Kapon kept in 'also'.
MRG Guyana page uses 'Patamona' (Ministry page spells 'Patomonas', already in 'also').
INE census PDF uses 'Pemón' with the accent.
Protected Areas Commission page uses 'Wai Wai'.
ISA page gives the self-name 'Wü Tarëno'; VIDS also writes 'Trio (Tiriyo, Tarëno)'.
ISA page uses 'Wajãpi' with the tilde.
ISA page: 'the Palikur use the term Parikwene' as self-reference.
INE census PDF: 'el pueblo que se auto-denomina ye'kwana'.
Pronunciamiento title uses 'Uwottüja' (body also has the variant 'Uwotjuja').
MinCultura PDF uses 'barí' with the accent.
AGN body text uses 'Parlamento del Pueblo Xinka' (headline uses the older 'xinca', kept in 'also').
ALMG grammar uses 'Ch'orti'' with both glottal marks.
